name: opencode-permission-rule-set
body: An agent's opencode 2.x permission model: one ordered `permissions` array of `{ action, resource, effect }` rules. opencode combines the rules in order — lower-priority configuration loads first, global rules are appended next, and agent rules are appended last — and the last matching rule wins, so an allow broadened by a later deny narrows again. Each rule carries an `action` (a tool or permission action; wildcards supported), a `resource` (path, command, URL, query, skill ID, or agent ID; wildcards supported), and an `effect` of `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`. A rule set in which no rule matches resolves to `ask`, and an operation that checks several resources (a patch touching several files) is denied if any `deny` matches, else asks if any `ask` matches, else is allowed. The documented action vocabulary is `read`, `edit` (edit, write, and patch), `glob`, `grep`, `shell`, `subagent`, `skill`, `question`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `external_directory`, `<server>_<tool>` for an MCP tool, and `execute`; the `subagent` action's resource is the target agent ID, and `external_directory` gates a path outside the active Location and its project worktree. The apg-suite tool grants appear as action rules under this vocabulary (the apg-suite tool actions alongside `shell`, `subagent`, and `edit`). `~`/`$HOME` is expanded for `read`, `edit`, and `external_directory` resources, and shell resources stay raw command text. Each distributed and generated agent carries one such rule set.
